messages.author: 79202ad2e866d5fa
messages.subject: batchProcess challenges
parts:
Hello,

I am working on a high resolution MSI dataset that was exported via fleximaging as a Analyze 7.5 file. I imported the file as "data" using data<-readAnalyze(name, folder, attach.only =TRUE)  wherein name and folder of course corresponded to my MSI file.
However, while using the batchProcess() function I obtained the following error:

> msset1 <- batchProcess(data, normalize=TRUE, smoothSignal=TRUE, reduceBaseline=TRUE, peakPick=list(SNR=10), peakAlign=TRUE)
batchProcess: normalize = TRUE
batchProcess: smoothSignal = TRUE
batchProcess: reduceBaseline = TRUE
batchProcess: peakPick = TRUE
batchProcess: peakAlign = TRUE
  |================================================| 100%
Error in if (!is.null(object@dim) && prod(object@dim) != object@length) errors <- c(errors,  : 
  missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
In addition: Warning message:
In x@dim[1] * length(j) : NAs produced by integer overflow

I've attempted to peakPick every 10th pixel as referenced in the manual however I'm unsure how to string multiple arguments with list() in batch processing. But I did try this:

> msset1 <- batchProcess(data, normalize=TRUE, smoothSignal=TRUE, reduceBaseline=TRUE, peakPick=list(pixel= seq(1, ncol(data), by 10), method="simple", SNR=10), peakAlign=TRUE, peakFilter=TRUE, reduceDimension=TRUE)
Error: unexpected numeric constant in "msset1 <- batchProcess(data, normalize=TRUE, smoothSignal=TRUE, reduceBaseline=TRUE, peakPick=list(pixel= seq(1, ncol(data), by 10"

My question is how can I process this large imaging file (~4.5gb) if at all?

messages.author: 6033d3c0e7d242fa
messages.subject: Re: batchProcess challenges
parts:
Hi Mark,

I will need to do some more testing to figure out what is going wrong with your first attempt to see if I can replicate it.

If you can print the output of traceback() after the error occurs, it may help me figure out the problem.

For the second, the problem is simply with your "seq()" call, where you need "by=10" instead of "by 10".

messages.author: 6033d3c0e7d242fa
messages.subject: Re: batchProcess challenges
parts:
Hi Mark,

imzML shouldn't typically be smaller than Analyze if they are being exported the same way (profile spectra) but may be much smaller if the spectra are processed in some way. I wouldn't spend a lot of time trying to make it work unless you want imzML for another reason besides file size.

I think I've figured out that problem though, which is not the file size itself, but that the number of data points is being computed with the wrong data type, causing the integer overflow. The fix is fairly simple on my end, but it may take me a little while to find time to push it.

(Bioconductor has switched their version control system again, so I will need to spend a weekend at some point fixing everything that broke.)

-Kylie
